# Wave 28c acceptance (`e5c6992..fc6978a`)

**Verdict: ACCEPT** - all 18 listed findings of the previous round are fixed in code; the four new items are minor/note.

## 1. Prior findings
- **D1 closed model list** - F42-1, F43-2 fixed. `Get-TelemetryModelToken` (`plugins/codex-consult/scripts/codex-consult-common.ps1:9619`) returns the table's own string on an exact `-ceq` after lower-casing, else `other`; `tags` is `[provider, model]` (:9695) and the title comes from `Get-TelemetryOutcome` (:9573). No free-text path into `details.model`, `tags` or `title` remains (README.md:2779, README.md:2791).
- **D2 `-Forget`** - F42-2, F43-1, F44-4 fixed. `Invoke-TelemetryForget` (:10569): `-PublicRef` alone never touches local state (:10594); with `-Local`, salt/spool/counters are removed only after `$r.Delivered` (:10630-10646), otherwise `& $undo` and exit 3 with nothing deleted; `-Local` alone states the intake still holds the data (:10584) and asks `[y/N]` unless `-Yes`.
- **D3 lock + marker** - F42-3 fixed. `Enter-TelemetryLock` (:9395) opens exclusively and checks the marker (:9402, :9411, :9418); the marker is written first (:10611) and removed last (:10646). After a crash it survives and the refusal text tells the operator to run `-Forget -Local` again (:9400); a re-run detects it (:10609).
- **D4 flush lock** - F42-7, F43-5, F44-2 fixed. Takeover only when the owner pid is gone or the lock names no owner (:10246-10250); the token is re-checked before each send and before the rewrite (:10428, :10438); the 5-minute age rule is gone and README.md:2870-2877 documents both the rule and the duplicate-on-lost-lock consequence.
- **D5 deadline** - F42-8 fixed: the clock is checked before enumeration, reads, each request and the rewrite (:10366-10440) with a 1 s reserve.
- **D6 sender environment** - F41-1, F42-9 fixed: allow list :9785-9793 adds `HTTP(S)_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `SSL_CERT_FILE/DIR`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`; per-OS casing :9809-9822.
- **D7 spool append** - F43-4 fixed: 1 s inside the task write lock (`codex-consult.ps1:5806`), 5 s retry after release (:5858), warning on console and in the status record only.
- **D8/D9 process trees** - F42-4, F42-5 fixed: `Get-PidIdentity` (`codex-consult-detached.ps1:168`) is three-state; an unverified pid is neither killed nor counted gone (:9115, :9140-9148); `Get-UnixDescendantTree` (:8681) treats a `pgrep` error as failed enumeration and falls back to `ps` then `/proc`.
- **D10 health journal** - F42-6, F44-1 fixed: unreadable lines move to `<journal>.bad` (:5340-5351), are counted in a warning (:5355, :5359), and truncation removes only what was applied or moved (:5362-5368).
- **D11 compaction** - F43-3, F44-6 fixed as far as the installed codex allows: `Get-CompactionCount` (:8523) feeds ledger `compactions` = n / `unknown` / null (:5321-5331); the prompt gains `Before you answer, re-read the brief: <path>.` (`codex-consult.ps1:4024`).
- **D12** F44-5 fixed: dry runs print the run warnings including the test-mode line (:3292, :4259).
- **D13** F43-7 fixed: CHANGELOG.md:1268-1271 corrects the 28b sentence; :1370-1373 records `19 harness(es), 0 failed` per host (implementer-reported; I did not re-run - RC1).
- **Accepted limitations** F43-6, F44-3: README.md:2796 states the vendor class "is derived from the host NAME only - a private gateway, relay or proxy under a vendor's" host reads as that vendor; README.md:2809 covers the `other` row. Confirmed documented. The derivation marker F43-6 proposed was not added (by decision).
- The F02/F03/F04/F15/F19/F22 ids predate this range (panel, routing, roles, quota work of earlier waves) and were not re-verified here: `not-checked`.

## 2. New defects in the areas named
- **Closed list**: no path left (above).
- **`-Forget`**: no exit path removes the salt without a confirmed DELETE when `-PublicRef` was given; the crash-left marker is self-healing.
- **Telemetry lock**: a producer holding it makes `-Forget` wait or refuse, never interleave. D4's no-owner deviation is safe: the identity is written inside the `CreateNew` handle held `FileShare::None` (:10225-10226), so a sender that is still starting can never be read as ownerless - only a writer that died between create and write leaves such a lock.
- **Deadline**: it cannot cut the rewrite (token/time checked before it, :10438-10440); the spool stays parseable, but the rewrite is `SetLength(0)` + in-place write (:10180-10186), so a crash in that window loses undelivered lines - finding #3.
- **Process tree**: "unconfirmed" can leave a bridge child running with no warning when a survivor also exists - finding #1 (minor).
- **Health journal**: concurrent `.bad` moves are serialized by the journal's exclusive open, and a failed `.bad` write keeps the lines in the journal (:5340-5351) - read, not executed.
- **Re-read-brief line**: added only when `context_tokens > 0` and a brief ref exists (:4024), before the `Consultation id` line; the routing seed is `-PanelSeed` / test hook / UTC date (:180, :2740-2741), not prompt text, and lineage is provider/model - so no prompt hash, seed or lineage change for any other reviewer.
- Finding #2: `Add-TelemetryNotSpooled` (:9938-9939) gives up silently after 1 s when the telemetry lock is busy. Finding #4: a living-but-hung lock owner wedges flushing indefinitely with no age fallback.

## 3. Verdict
**ACCEPT.** No blocker or major remains. Finding #1 is a two-line wording change (name `Unverified` in the survivor message and record it) and can land after release; #2-#4 are notes.

## Requested checks
- **RC1** - repo root, workspace-write, ~20 min: `tests/run-all.ps1` under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh at `fc6978a`; expect `19 harness(es), 0 failed` on both (settles D13/F43-7 and the ask-10 counts).
- **RC2** - repo root, workspace-write, ~10 min: with `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1` point `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` at a closed loopback port and run `codex-telemetry.ps1 -Forget -PublicRef ref1 -Local -Yes`; expect exit 3 and the salt still present, then `-Forget -PublicRef ref1` again expecting a real DELETE attempt (not exit 1 "no instance id") - settles D2/F43-1.

findings.claim: D8's unverified descendants are left running and are named nowhere when the same kill also has a survivor: `Add-KillCheck` warns only when `Survivors.Count -eq 0` (codex-consult.ps1:1745), `Format-KillText` returns `(process tree killed)` whenever survivors exist (:1760), and the survivor `Problem` text (:1849) plus the recovery record (`state=survivors`, `survivors` built from `$surv` only, :1852-1853) list only the alive pids - so a descendant whose start time could not be read (never killed: common.ps1:9115 `continue`; recorded only in `Unverified`/`Why`, common.ps1:9145-9148) is invisible to the operator and to recovery, even though `kill_confirmed` is correctly false.
findings.trigger: A timeout (or `-Kick`) kill where the tree contains both a descendant that is confirmed alive after 3 s and one whose start time is unreadable - e.g. a shell child plus an elevated/other-user grandchild on Windows, or a `/proc`-restricted pid on Linux.

evidence.observation: `Add-KillCheck` gates the warning on `-not $Check.Confirmed -and @($Check.Survivors).Count -eq 0`; `Get-KillMayRunPids` (which does prefer `Unverified`) is therefore only reached in the no-survivor case, and `Format-KillText` short-circuits to `(process tree killed)` when survivors exist.

With survivors, `$t.Problem` is rebuilt as `(process tree killed; N processes survived: pid ...)` from `$surv` alone and `$pendingRecord.survivors` is built from `New-SurvivorEntries -Pids $surv`; `Unverified` is not referenced.

The kill loop skips any pid whose identity is not `alive`, so unverified descendants are deliberately not killed; they are returned only in `$res.Unverified` / `$res.Why`, and `$res.Survivors` holds the alive set - both sets can be non-empty at once.

findings.verification: Fake a timeout kill with one descendant that survives and one whose start time cannot be read (test hook or an other-user child), then read the console warning, the ledger `Problem`/`kill_confirmed` and the pending record's `survivors`: the unverified pid appears in none of them.
findings.remedy: Include `Unverified` in the survivor wording and in the recovery record: emit the `kill not confirmed ... pid <unverified> may still run` warning whenever `Unverified.Count -gt 0` (not only when there are no survivors), and add the unverified pids to `$pendingRecord.survivors` (flagged `unverified`) so recovery names them.

findings.claim: `Add-TelemetryNotSpooled` takes the telemetry lock with `-WaitMs 1000` and returns silently when it cannot (`if (-not $lk.Ok) { return }`), so the not-spooled counter loses exactly the events whose drop it exists to count - and the most likely reason for a >1 s busy lock is a concurrent `-Forget -Local` (which holds the lock while the DELETE runs, :10559) or a slow-volume append by another panel member. The per-run console warning still fires, so the loss is only in `-Status`'s count.
findings.trigger: Telemetry on, a commit whose spool append fails, and the telemetry lock held for more than 1 s at that moment (a `-Forget -Local` in flight, or four panel members committing on a slow volume).

evidence.observation: `Enter-TelemetryLock -WaitMs 1000 -IgnoreMarker` followed by `if (-not $lk.Ok) { return }` with no fallback write and no diagnostic.
`Add-TelemetryEvent` calls `Add-TelemetryNotSpooled -Why $r.Why` only when `-Count` is set, so a dropped count is unrecoverable later.

findings.verification: Hold the telemetry lock from a second process for 3 s while a fake consultation commits with `-Count`; then run `codex-telemetry.ps1 -Status` and confirm `not spooled: none` although the run warned that the event was not spooled.
findings.remedy: Retry the count append outside the lock (it is a separate file) or with the same 5 s budget the second spool attempt uses, and if it still fails say so in the run warning instead of returning silently.

findings.claim: `Remove-TelemetrySpoolLines` rewrites the spool in place (`$fs.SetLength(0)` then one write, :10180-10186) with no temp-file-and-rename, so a crash or kill inside that window loses every kept line of that day's spool (undelivered events and complaints) with no counter; the D5 deadline does not cut the rewrite (the token/time check precedes it, :10438-10440) but it does not make it durable either.
findings.trigger: The detached sender is killed, or the host loses power, between `SetLength(0)` and `Flush()` of a spool that still holds undelivered lines.

evidence.observation: Lines to keep are collected in memory, then the same handle truncates the file to zero and rewrites it; there is no temporary file, no rename, and no record of the pre-rewrite line count.
The rewrite runs after a `Test-TelemetryFlushLockMine` check with `-WaitMs` bounded by the remaining deadline, confirming the deadline gates entry to the rewrite but not the rewrite itself.

findings.verification: Start a flush against a fake intake with a spool of several lines, kill the sender during the rewrite (or inject a fault at :10180 in a test copy), then count the spool lines: expect 0 rather than the undelivered remainder.
findings.remedy: Write the kept lines to `<spool>.tmp` and rename over the original (or append a `rewrite` marker line the next sender can detect), and record the kept-line count in `.last` so a loss is countable.

findings.claim: With the 5-minute age rule removed, a flush lock whose owner process still exists is never taken over - including an owner that is suspended (sleep, hibernation, debugger) or one whose start time is unreadable, since `Test-PidAlive` counts `unknown` as alive - so all telemetry flushing for that spool stops indefinitely; the only remedy is killing the owner pid by hand or deleting `.flush.lock`, and neither is documented as the remedy (README.md:2872-2877 only reports `sender busy since <t> (pid <n> holds its lock, <s> s old - its owner lives: left alone)`).
findings.trigger: A detached sender is suspended mid-flush (laptop sleep, VM pause, debugger) and never resumes, or its recorded `start_time` becomes unreadable while its pid lives; every later run then refuses to flush.

evidence.observation: `$stale` is set only for `opid <= 0` or a dead owner; a living owner returns `Why` with `left alone` and no age-based fallback remains.
`Test-PidAlive` returns true whenever a process with the pid exists and the recorded start time is empty or unreadable - documented as "never taken over on a guess".

The lock rules and the busy message are documented, including "an owner whose identity cannot be confirmed counts as living" and "The 5-minute age rule of wave 28b is gone", but no operator recovery step is given.

findings.verification: Write a `.flush.lock` naming a living pid with an empty `start_time` (or suspend a real sender), run a fake consultation with telemetry on, and confirm every flush refuses with `left alone` for as long as the pid lives; check `-Status` and README for a stated remedy.
findings.remedy: Keep the no-takeover rule but document the recovery (`stop pid <n>` or delete `<spool>/.flush.lock`) in the refusal text and in README, and report the busy-sender age in `-Status` so an operator can see a wedge growing.

first_run_checklist: First committed consultation with telemetry on: no `telemetry event not spooled` warning on the console, and `codex-telemetry.ps1 -Status` shows the event count incremented with `not spooled: none`.
`-Status` shows no `forgetting :` marker; if one is present the run's refusal text names it and `-Forget -Local` must be re-run to finish before telemetry resumes.

A reviewer whose roster entry sets `context_tokens`: the ledger carries `compactions` (`unknown` or a number, never absent) and the prompt's last-but-one line is `Before you answer, re-read the brief: <path>.`; any compaction warning means the reply may rest on a summary - check it answers every numbered ask.

Any timeout or `-Kick` kill: `(process tree killed)` appears only with `kill_confirmed: true`; when it is false the console names the pid(s) that may still run - and if survivors are also listed, look for the unverified pid by hand (finding #1 says the bridge will not name it).
`kill_confirmed: false` on a timed-out turn must mean no continuation turn was started (recovery state `survivors` keeps the pending record).
If `health journal: N unreadable line(s) kept in <file>` appears, confirm `<health>.journal.bad` holds those lines and the journal was truncated only by what was applied or moved.

`-Status` reports a last-flush result; a `.flush.lock` reported as `sender busy since <t> (pid <n> ... left alone)` with a pid that is not an active sender means telemetry is wedged - kill that pid or remove the lock (finding #4).
The routing record of a panel run (`panel.routing`) is unchanged in shape and the seed/nonce still comes from `-PanelSeed`, the test hook or the UTC date - not from the new prompt line.
